answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x and isolated to the primary region during peak settlement, so the closest analog is the March regional failover that restored latency in minutes without dropping traffic. Rollback is disallowed by the security-patch constraint, so memory_b1 is used only as a negative. Circuit breaking would fail fast and risks losing customer writes, which violates the objective. Read-replica routing previously helped when report reads contended with writes, but the live symptom is the write path under settlement load, not dashboards; verifying memory_b5 checks whether that mechanism could still unload the primary without moving writes. Pre-peak capacity (memory_b3) is a weaker fit mid-incident. Failover at settlement peak can still perturb downstream settlement if the shift is unclean, so that risk is flagged and scale stays short of a full untested cutover until the archive confirms memory_b2.
